editorial:
Ever wonder how the music in a movie makes you feel so stressed out or excited? You get a front-row seat to that process here. You will see composer Daniel Lopatin and director Josh Safdie chatting about the wild sounds they created for Uncut Gems. It is not your typical boring music lesson. Instead, it feels like a backstage pass where you see exactly how they used a huge synthesizer called the Moog One to make those loud, pulsing beats that keep you on the edge of your seat. The vibe is very chill and creative, making you feel like you are just hanging out in a studio with two pros.

What really works is how Lopatin shows you the actual buttons and knobs he turned to get those specific sounds. It is great because you don't need to be a musician to enjoy it. If you loved the tension in the original movie, you will love seeing how that stress was built through sound. My only complaint is that it is quite short, but it packs a punch. You should definitely watch this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see the gear clearly, or maybe grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection if you love high-quality audio.
endingExplained: The documentary wraps up by showing how all the separate synth sounds come together for the film's biggest scenes. Lopatin explains that the music had to match the main character's chaotic life. It ends with a look at the final tracks, proving that the music was just as important as the acting. You walk away understanding that the sounds were meant to feel like a ticking clock that never stops until the very end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music production or the movie Uncut Gems.
